payload.markdown:
A kiosk that opens late loses the 10:00 rush. A kiosk that closes sloppy carries cooked pearls into tomorrow, and the SOP is clear that cooked pearls are made fresh every day and thrown away at close.

Your SOP splits the day into two checklists. Section 3 of the SOP sets the shifts:

| Shift | Hours | Arrive by | Runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Opening | 10:00 to 16:00 | 09:30 | Opening checklist (section 4) |
| Closing | 16:00 to 22:30 | 15:50 | Closing checklist (section 5) |

The opening shift arrives at 09:30 with thirty minutes before the doors open. That half hour is not slack: it holds the handwash, the uniform, the chiller and freezer readings, the date labels, the first batch of pearls (about 50 minutes), the tea, the ice, sanitising and the sealer test. Skip one and you either open late or open with equipment that has not been verified.

The closing shift arrives at 15:50 and finishes at 22:30. The shop closes at 22:00, but the closing checklist runs from 21:30 to 22:30 because the last hour is where the cut-offs live: stop cooking new pearls at 21:30, last orders at 21:55, and every cooked pearl in the pot goes in the bin before you lock up. The SOP is explicit that cooked pearls, brewed tea and opened fresh milk and oat milk are prepared fresh every day — they are discarded, not stored.

Two failures the checklists exist to prevent: a bar opened without anyone washing their hands, and pearls carried into the next day. Both are invisible at the time.

payload.intro: The opening checklist is section 4 of the SOP, run from 09:30 so the kiosk opens at 10:00. Each step below is one bullet of section 4, in the SOP's order, with the [LAW] or [SHOP] tag the SOP prints beside it.

steps.title: Wash your hands with soap for at least 20 seconds
steps.detail_markdown: Do this before touching anything behind the bar. [LAW, reg. 33(1)(c)]
steps.warning: Starting the pearl pot first because it takes longest means everything you touched on the way in is now on the pot handle.
steps.check: Hands washed with soap for a counted 20 seconds before anything behind the bar is touched.

steps.title: Put on the uniform and take off jewellery
steps.detail_markdown: Shop T-shirt, light-coloured apron, cap, closed shoes. Remove rings, watches, bracelets and pins. [LAW, regs. 32 and 33(1)(f)]
steps.warning: A ring or watch behind the bar breaks reg. 33(1)(f), whatever the shift.
steps.check: Apron, cap and closed shoes on; nothing on your fingers or wrists.

steps.title: Read the chiller and freezer thermometers and log both
steps.detail_markdown: Write both readings in the temperature log. The chiller must be 4 °C or below, the freezer -18 °C or below. If the chiller is above 5 °C, tell the shift lead before using any milk. [SHOP]
steps.warning: Writing a number you did not read makes the log useless: the 5 °C rule only works if the reading is real.
steps.check: Two readings in the log; a chiller above 5 °C has gone to the shift lead before any milk is used.

steps.title: Check date labels
steps.detail_markdown: Throw away anything past its use-by time and record it in the waste log. Use stock first in, first out. [LAW, reg. 38(1)(i)]
steps.warning: An expired item left on the shelf goes into the first drink that needs it.
steps.check: Nothing past its use-by time; every discard in the waste log.

steps.title: Start the first batch of pearls
steps.detail_markdown: Follow section 6.1. A batch takes about 50 minutes, so start it first, before the tea.
steps.warning: A late pot means no ready pearls at 10:00, and the 25-minute rest in step 3 of section 6.1 cannot be skipped.
steps.check: The pearl water is at a rolling boil or the pearls are cooking.

steps.title: Brew the teas and check the syrup
steps.detail_markdown: Brew black tea and jasmine green tea (section 6.2). Check the brown sugar syrup; make more if the bottle is under half full (section 6.3).
steps.warning: Steeping too long makes the tea bitter: black tea 8 minutes, jasmine green tea 6 minutes.
steps.check: Both teas strained into the urn and labelled with the time; syrup bottle at least half full.

steps.title: Fill the ice bin with the ice scoop
steps.detail_markdown: Never scoop ice with a cup or your hands. Leave the scoop in its holder, handle up. [SHOP; ice must be protected from contamination, LAW reg. 35(1)(j)]
steps.warning: A cup used as a scoop can chip into the ice, and hands contaminate it.
steps.check: Ice bin full; scoop in its holder, handle up.

steps.title: Sanitise the counter and equipment
steps.detail_markdown: Sanitise the counter, shakers, jugs and the sealing machine plate.
steps.warning: Last night's wash does not cover what touched the counter since.
steps.check: Counter, shakers, jugs and sealing plate sanitised.

steps.title: Load the cup film and test the sealer
steps.detail_markdown: Load the cup film and test the sealing machine on an empty cup.
steps.warning: An untested sealer is found out on the first customer's drink.
steps.check: An empty test cup sealed flat and tight.

steps.title: Set up the counter and open at 10:00
steps.detail_markdown: Turn on the POS, check the RM 200 float in the cash drawer, put out the DuitNow QR stand, the menu and the allergen board. Open at 10:00.
steps.warning: Opening without the allergen board leaves the cashier without the one thing section 9 says to check with the customer.
steps.check: POS on, RM 200 float counted, QR stand, menu and allergen board out, doors open at 10:00.

payload.title: Closing checklist, 21:30 to 22:30

items.why: Anything started after 21:30 cannot be sold before close and must be discarded.
Orders after 21:55 cannot be made and cleaned up before 22:30.

items.text: All cooked pearls, brewed tea, opened fresh milk and oat milk thrown away and recorded in the waste log
items.why: These are prepared fresh every day; carrying them overnight is the failure this checklist exists to prevent.

items.text: Shakers, jugs, scoops and the pearl pot washed with detergent, rinsed, sanitised, air-dried upside down
items.why: Detergent residue left on a shaker taints the first drink of the next shift.

items.text: Sealing machine unplugged; sealing plate wiped only once cool
items.why: Wiping a hot plate burns you and warps the plate.

items.text: Ice bin emptied, wiped dry, lid left open
items.why: A closed, damp ice bin grows mould overnight.

items.text: All food put away or covered BEFORE sweeping and mopping
items.why: Sweeping near open food is a food-safety breach.

items.text: Counters, POS screen and menu boards wiped; floor swept and mopped
items.why: Sticky counters and screens are the first thing the morning shift touches.

items.text: Rubbish taken to the bin centre and new bin liners put in
items.why: Rubbish left overnight in a warm kiosk attracts pests.

items.text: Chiller and freezer temperatures written in the log
items.why: A gap in the log is treated as an unmonitored unit.

items.text: Cash drawer counted with the shift lead and POS closed
items.why: A drawer counted alone cannot be reconciled against a dispute.

items.text: Lights, water heater and tea urn switched off, shop locked, photo of the completed checklist posted in the crew group chat
items.why: The photo is the only proof the checklist was actually run.

payload.note: The SOP states cooked pearls, brewed tea and opened fresh milk and oat milk are prepared fresh every day and are discarded at close. There is no 'keep it for tomorrow' option. If you are unsure whether something was opened today, throw it away and log it.

payload.belief: If I stop cooking pearls at 21:30 but there are still pearls in the pot at 22:00, I can leave them for the opening shift to use first thing tomorrow.
payload.why_it_seems_right: The pearls look and smell fine, the pot is covered, and throwing away food that was cooked ninety minutes ago feels wasteful. On a busy night there can be a full pot left, and binning it feels like admitting you cooked too many.
payload.what_is_true: The SOP states that cooked pearls, brewed tea and opened fresh milk and oat milk are prepared fresh every day and are discarded at close. There is no keep-for-tomorrow option, however good they look; section 6.1 already limits cooked pearls to 4 hours in the warmer. The waste log exists so that over-cooking shows up as a number the manager can act on, instead of as a pot someone quietly keeps.

assessments.prompt: The closing checklist says to put all food away or cover it before sweeping and mopping. Explain why the order matters, and name one other closing step whose timing is forced by a temperature or a cut-off.

answer_key.reference_answer: Sweeping and mopping lift dust and floor debris into the air, which can settle on open food, so food must be covered or stored first. Other steps with forced timing: stop cooking new pearls at 21:30, last orders at 21:55, wipe the sealing plate only when it is cool, and unplug the sealing machine before cleaning it.

rubric.acceptable: Says food must be put away first to keep it clean, without naming the airborne route.
rubric.poor: Says the order does not matter or repeats the rule without any reason.

rubric.acceptable: Names a step such as unplugging the sealing machine but does not state the time or condition that forces it.

payload.title: Run one opening and one closing under observation
payload.brief_markdown:
You have read both checklists. Now run them.

**Scenario.** You are on the opening shift on a Tuesday and the closing shift on the same day. A shift lead watches both and signs off.

**Constraints.**
- Opening: arrive by 09:30, doors open at 10:00. You may not skip a step to make the time — if you are behind, the shift lead decides what to cut, not you.
- Closing: the 21:30 pearl cut-off and the 21:55 last-orders cut-off are hard. You may not serve a drink after 21:55 and you may not start a pearl batch after 21:30.
- Every discard goes in the waste log with an amount, including anything you throw away because you were unsure whether it was opened today.
- The photo of the completed closing checklist goes in the crew group chat before you lock up (section 5).

**Done looks like.** Two completed checklists, both photographed and posted, with no step marked done that you did not actually do, and a waste log entry for every discard.
deliverables: A completed opening checklist with both thermometer readings in the temperature log and the RM 200 float checked, signed off by the shift lead before 10:00.
A completed closing checklist with the 21:30 and 21:55 cut-offs confirmed, photographed and posted before you leave.
A waste log entry for every pearl, tea, milk and oat milk discard, with amounts.
A 100-word note for the shift lead naming the one step you nearly missed and what made you nearly miss it.

assessments.prompt: Run one full opening checklist and one full closing checklist under a shift lead's observation, produce both completed checklists with photographs, and write the 100-word note on the step you nearly missed.

answer_key.reference_answer: A passing submission shows both checklists completed in SOP order with real readings and times, both cut-offs respected, every discard logged with an amount, both photos posted, and a note that names a specific step and the specific reason it was nearly missed.

rubric.criterion: Opening checklist run in SOP order with real readings and times
rubric.excellent: Handwashing happens before any food-contact surface is touched, both chiller and freezer readings are written with the time they were taken, and the doors open at 10:00 only after the checklist is complete.
rubric.acceptable: All steps are done but one is out of order, or a reading is written without its time.
rubric.poor: A step is skipped, a reading is copied rather than taken, or the doors open before the checklist is complete.

rubric.criterion: Closing cut-offs respected and discards logged
rubric.excellent: No pearl batch is started after 21:30, no drink is served after 21:55, and every pearl, tea, milk and oat milk discard has a waste log entry with an amount.
rubric.acceptable: Cut-offs are respected but one discard is missing an amount or was logged after the fact without a number.
rubric.poor: A cut-off is broken, or cooked pearls or opened milk are kept for the next day.

rubric.criterion: Both checklists photographed and posted to the crew group chat
rubric.excellent: Two photos, one per shift, posted at the end of each shift and readable enough to confirm every tick.
rubric.acceptable: Both photos are posted but one is blurry or posted the next morning.
rubric.poor: One or both photos are missing.

rubric.criterion: Note names a specific near-miss step and its cause
rubric.excellent: Names one step, states the concrete reason it was nearly missed, and says what would have caught it.
rubric.acceptable: Names a step but the reason given is general, such as being busy.
rubric.poor: Says nothing was nearly missed, or names no step.
